title: Grade 4 SOCIAL STUDIES — Premium Revision Paper #18

pages.quiz:
SOCIAL STUDIES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #18
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these is a cardinal point? (1 mark)
   A. North-west
   B. South-west
   C. North-east
   D. West

2. What does a compass needle point to? (1 mark)
   A. The nearest town
   B. North
   C. South
   D. The sun

3. Which county borders Uganda? (1 mark)
   A. Kitui
   B. Nairobi
   C. Nyeri
   D. Busia

4. On a physical map, what colour is used for water? (1 mark)
   A. Black
   B. Blue
   C. Brown
   D. Red

5. Which lake is the largest lake in Africa and is shared by Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania? (1 mark)
   A. Lake Naivasha
   B. Lake Victoria
   C. Lake Baringo
   D. Lake Nakuru

6. What would you draw as a symbol for a river on a map? (1 mark)
   A. A black circle
   B. A green triangle
   C. A wavy blue line
   D. A red square

7. Why should a weather chart be filled in at the same time each day? (1 mark)
   A. So that the sun rises earlier
   B. So that the records can be compared fairly
   C. So that the chart looks big
   D. So that rain stops

8. What is an artefact? (1 mark)
   A. A type of weather
   B. A mountain
   C. A river
   D. An object made and used by people in the past

9. What is the name of the organisation that looks after most museums in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. National Museums of Kenya
   B. Kenya Power
   C. Kenya Ports
   D. Kenya Airways

10. Which place is used mainly for prayers and worship? (1 mark)
   A. Hospital
   B. Church, mosque or temple
   C. Factory
   D. Market

11. What is population? (1 mark)
   A. The rainfall in a place
   B. The size of a place
   C. The number of people living in a place
   D. The number of animals in a place

12. Which of these is not a reason for crowded areas? (1 mark)
   A. Good roads
   B. Very little rain and no water
   C. Fertile soil
   D. Jobs in a town

13. Which is the best way to show population on a map using dots? (1 mark)
   A. Draw dots where people live and give a key for what a dot means
   B. Colour the whole map blue
   C. Draw a river
   D. Write the county name only

14. Which is a ceremony? (1 mark)
   A. A market
   B. A rainy day
   C. A wedding
   D. A road

15. Why is it important to check facts before telling your school's history? (1 mark)
   A. So that it is funny
   B. So that nobody listens
   C. So that the story is longer
   D. So that what you tell is true

16. What is mining? (1 mark)
   A. Catching fish
   B. Cutting hair
   C. Taking minerals from the ground
   D. Growing maize

17. Which is a way of conserving water? (1 mark)
   A. Leaving taps running
   B. Cutting trees near rivers
   C. Polluting rivers
   D. Turning off taps after use

18. What is a resource? (1 mark)
   A. A school rule
   B. A kind of weather
   C. A game
   D. Something we can use to meet our needs and earn a living

19. Which of these is a jua kali product? (1 mark)
   A. A satellite
   B. A big ship
   C. A jet plane
   D. A metal door made in a small workshop

20. Why are sugar factories usually built near cane farms? (1 mark)
   A. Farmers do not like factories
   B. Cane is heavy and costly to carry far
   C. Cane is hard to find
   D. Sugar cannot be sold

21. What raw material is used in a cement factory? (1 mark)
   A. Fish
   B. Sugarcane
   C. Limestone
   D. Milk

22. Which of these is a benefit of industries? (1 mark)
   A. They provide jobs
   B. They close schools
   C. They remove roads
   D. They stop trade

23. In school life, what is a right? (1 mark)
   A. Something you are allowed to have or do
   B. A punishment
   C. A rule to break
   D. A duty you refuse

24. Which action shows responsibility? (1 mark)
   A. Breaking things
   B. Doing your class duty without being reminded
   C. Refusing to help
   D. Waiting to be told each time

25. Which day is the International Day of Peace? (1 mark)
   A. 12 December
   B. 21 September
   C. 25 December
   D. 1 January

26. What is the Kiswahili word for peace? (1 mark)
   A. Chakula
   B. Shule
   C. Rafiki
   D. Amani

27. If you see a pupil being bullied, what should you do? (1 mark)
   A. Laugh
   B. Tell a trusted adult and support the pupil
   C. Join in
   D. Ignore

28. What is a conflict? (1 mark)
   A. A disagreement or quarrel
   B. A book
   C. A holiday
   D. A song

29. What is a peace corner? (1 mark)
   A. A shop
   B. A quiet place to calm down or talk through a problem
   C. A place to fight
   D. A place to hide

30. Which of these is a child right? (1 mark)
   A. To be beaten
   B. To work in a quarry
   C. To go to school
   D. To be married early

31. What is a responsibility? (1 mark)
   A. A toy
   B. A duty you should do
   C. A gift
   D. A secret

32. Whose fault is it if a child is abused? (1 mark)
   A. The child
   B. The teacher only
   C. The abuser, never the child
   D. The neighbour

33. What is child abuse? (1 mark)
   A. Playing with a child
   B. Feeding a child
   C. Teaching a child
   D. Treating a child in a way that harms the child

34. Which is a responsibility of a child? (1 mark)
   A. Bully others
   B. Steal
   C. Skip school
   D. Respect others and study hard

35. At what age can a Kenyan vote in national elections? (1 mark)
   A. 12 years
   B. 15 years
   C. 18 years
   D. 10 years

36. What is a candidate? (1 mark)
   A. A cleaner
   B. A teacher
   C. A voter
   D. A person who stands to be elected

37. Who leads a clan? (1 mark)
   A. A bus driver
   B. A footballer
   C. Clan elders
   D. A cook

38. What is devolution? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of tax
   B. Ending the government
   C. Keeping all power in one place
   D. Sharing power and resources between the national and county governments

39. How often are governors elected? (1 mark)
   A. Every twenty years
   B. Every month
   C. Every five years
   D. Every year

40. Where does a county government get money? (1 mark)
   A. Only from gifts
   B. Only from fines
   C. From nowhere
   D. From the national government and local fees and taxes

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Describe how to stay safe during a visit to a factory. Give four rules. (4 marks)

42. Explain why many families live near towns and rivers. (3 marks)

43. Explain how you can stay calm when you feel very angry. (3 marks)

44. On a sketch map the school is in the middle, the market is above it and the clinic is below it. Write two sentences to say where the market and the clinic are. (4 marks)

45. Explain why a Children's Government should not punish pupils. (3 marks)

46. Using time words, write a short history of a school that opened in 1985 and built a library in 2000. (3 marks)

47. Give two examples of goods and two examples of services. (4 marks)

48. Describe three problems that crowded areas can have and one way of reducing each. (5 marks)

49. Explain why the county assembly must check the work of the governor. (5 marks)

50. List four democratic processes in a school. (4 marks)

51. Name three child rights. (3 marks)

52. Explain the difference between clustered and scattered settlement. (3 marks)

53. A weather chart for a week shows: Mon sunny, Tue sunny, Wed rainy, Thu cloudy, Fri rainy, Sat sunny, Sun cloudy. How many days were sunny, rainy and cloudy? (3 marks)

54. Name three natural resources found in Kenya and say how each is used. (3 marks)

55. Plan a class culture day. State five things you would include. (5 marks)

56. Give three school values and say why each is important. (3 marks)

57. What is the difference between a lake and a river? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #18 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — West
   Only north, east, south and west are cardinal points. The others are in-between points.

2. B — North
   A magnetic compass needle always turns to point north.

3. D — Busia
   Busia is on the border with Uganda.

4. B — Blue
   Blue is used for lakes, rivers and the ocean.

5. B — Lake Victoria
   Lake Victoria is shared by three countries.

6. C — A wavy blue line
   Rivers are shown as wavy blue lines.

7. B — So that the records can be compared fairly
   Observing at the same time gives fair comparisons.

8. D — An object made and used by people in the past
   Artefacts include tools, pots and clothes.

9. A — National Museums of Kenya
   The National Museums of Kenya manages many museums.

10. B — Church, mosque or temple
   Places of worship are for prayer.

11. C — The number of people living in a place
   Population is the number of people in an area.

12. B — Very little rain and no water
   Dryness with no water makes areas sparse.

13. A — Draw dots where people live and give a key for what a dot means
   A dot map needs a clear key.

14. C — A wedding
   A wedding is a special event with customs.

15. D — So that what you tell is true
   History must be accurate.

16. C — Taking minerals from the ground
   Mining takes minerals such as soda ash or titanium from the earth.

17. D — Turning off taps after use
   Saving water helps everyone.

18. D — Something we can use to meet our needs and earn a living
   Resources include land, water, minerals and people's skills.

19. D — A metal door made in a small workshop
   Jua kali workers make goods like doors and furniture.

20. B — Cane is heavy and costly to carry far
   Being near saves transport costs.

21. C — Limestone
   Cement is made using limestone.

22. A — They provide jobs
   Industries employ people.

23. A — Something you are allowed to have or do
   Rights are things we are allowed, such as learning.

24. B — Doing your class duty without being reminded
   Responsible pupils do their duties.

25. B — 21 September
   The International Day of Peace is on 21 September.

26. D — Amani
   Amani means peace.

27. B — Tell a trusted adult and support the pupil
   Reporting helps to stop bullying.

28. A — A disagreement or quarrel
   A conflict is a disagreement.

29. B — A quiet place to calm down or talk through a problem
   A peace corner helps pupils settle problems.

30. C — To go to school
   Children have the right to education.

31. B — A duty you should do
   Rights come with responsibilities.

32. C — The abuser, never the child
   Abuse is never the child's fault.

33. D — Treating a child in a way that harms the child
   Abuse harms a child's body, feelings or future.

34. D — Respect others and study hard
   Rights come with responsibilities.

35. C — 18 years
   Adults aged 18 and above can vote.

36. D — A person who stands to be elected
   Candidates ask for votes.

37. C — Clan elders
   Clan elders lead the clan.

38. D — Sharing power and resources between the national and county governments
   Devolution moves some power to counties.

39. C — Every five years
   General elections are held every five years.

40. D — From the national government and local fees and taxes
   Counties get shared money and collect local fees.

SECTION B
----
41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Stay with the group, do not touch machines, listen to the guide, and wear safety clothing if given.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Towns have jobs, schools and shops. Rivers give water for drinking and farming. These things make life easier.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for towns, 1 mark for rivers, 1 mark for making life easier.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Walk away, take slow deep breaths, and count to ten before speaking.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: The market is north of the school. The clinic is south of the school.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct direction word and 1 mark for each correct sentence.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Only teachers decide on discipline, pupil leaders may be unfair, and serious problems must be reported to teachers.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: The school was opened in 1985. Later, in 2000, a library was built. Today, pupils read books in the library.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for dates, 1 mark for order, 1 mark for time words.

47. (4 marks)
   Answer: Goods: maize and shoes. Services: teaching and nursing.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct example.

48. (5 marks)
   Answer: Shortage of houses: build more houses. Litter: organise cleaning and waste collection. Traffic: improve roads and public transport. Award marks for each problem and each solution.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each problem/solution pair, up to 5 marks.

49. (5 marks)
   Answer: To make sure county money is used honestly, to prevent misuse of power, to make sure services reach people, to protect citizens' interests, and to keep the governor accountable.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid reason.

50. (4 marks)
   Answer: Electing class monitors, class meetings, using a suggestion box, and voting on decisions.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each process.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: The right to education, to health care and to protection. Accept food, a name or play.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each right.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: Clustered means homes are close together in a group, for example around a town. Scattered means homes are far apart from each other.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 mark for a clear contrast.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: 3 sunny days, 2 rainy days and 2 cloudy days.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct count. Check: 3 + 2 + 2 = 7 days.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: Water is used for drinking and farming. Land is used for farming and grazing. Minerals such as soda ash are used in factories.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each resource with a use.

55. (5 marks)
   Answer: Traditional dress, foods to taste, songs and dances, artefacts on display, and stories told by elders.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct item.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: Honesty helps us to be trusted. Respect keeps peace. Responsibility helps us to do our duties. Accept other valid values.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each value with a reason.

57. (2 marks)
   Answer: A lake is a large area of water with land around it. A river is water flowing along a channel to a lake or ocean.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct description.
